hook.line: Running a café means planning around other people: leave the note where Vale will see it, finish before the lawyer arrives, say nothing so nobody panics. Spanish has three small words for exactly that.
hook.es: Lo dejo aquí para que lo veas.
hook.en: I'll leave it here so you can see it. (to a friend)

rule:
Three small phrases link what one person does to what another person does:
*para que* so that
*sin que* without
*antes de que* before

The second action belongs to someone else, so its verb takes the wish form: *veas*, *note*, *salgas*, *llegue*. You met it with *cuando*. Look at the endings: *-ar* verbs switch to *-e*, the others to *-a*.

When the same person does both things, drop *que* and use the plain verb: *Abro temprano para encontrar todo listo.* *Llámame antes de salir.*
smallPrint: Teachers call this the subjunctive after purpose and time conjunctions. It is the same wish form, now used for plans that involve someone else.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *para* or *sin* and type the whole sentence: *Lo dejo aquí ___ que lo veas.* (I'll leave it here so you can see it, to a friend.)
yourTurn.answer: Lo dejo aquí para que lo veas.
yourTurn.why: You leave it so that the other person sees it, so *para que*.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *para* or *sin* and type the whole sentence: *Hernando entra ___ que nadie lo note.* (Hernando walks in without anyone noticing him.)
yourTurn.answer: Hernando entra sin que nadie lo note.
yourTurn.why: "Without" is *sin que*, followed by the wish form *note*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish, to a friend: Call me before you leave.
accept: Llámame antes de que te vayas.
yourTurn.why: *Antes de que* needs the *de*, then the wish form *salgas*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: I open early so that Vale finds everything ready.
yourTurn.answer: Abro temprano para que Vale encuentre todo listo.
accept: Yo abro temprano para que Vale encuentre todo listo.
yourTurn.why: Vale is the one finding, so *para que* and *encuentre*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Tomás leaves before the lawyer arrives.
yourTurn.answer: Tomás se va antes de que llegue la abogada.
accept: Tomás se va antes de que la abogada llegue.
yourTurn.why: The lawyer arrives, so *antes de que* and *llegue*.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it about one person only: *Abro temprano para que Vale encuentre todo listo.* Say: I open early to find everything ready.
yourTurn.answer: Abro temprano para encontrar todo listo.
accept: Yo abro temprano para encontrar todo listo.
yourTurn.why: When the same person does both things, *que* disappears and the verb stays plain.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Nobody signs anything without Tomás reading it.
yourTurn.answer: Nadie firma nada sin que lo lea Tomás.
accept: Nadie firma nada sin que Tomás lo lea.
yourTurn.why: *Sin que* plus the wish form *lea*, because Tomás is the one reading.

pitfalls.wrong: Lo dejo aquí para que lo ves.
pitfalls.right: Lo dejo aquí para que lo veas.
pitfalls.why: Almost. After *para que* the verb takes its wish form: *veas*, not *ves*.
Almost. The phrase is *antes de que*, with the *de*.

pitfalls.wrong: Hernando entra sin nadie lo note.
pitfalls.right: Hernando entra sin que nadie lo note.
pitfalls.why: Almost. When someone else does the second action, *sin* needs *que*.

pitfalls.wrong: Abro temprano para que yo encuentre todo listo.
pitfalls.right: Abro temprano para encontrar todo listo.
pitfalls.why: Almost. If you do both things yourself, skip *que* and use the plain verb.

personal: Say one thing you do so that someone else can do something, or without someone noticing, using *para que* or *sin que*.
